note: Draft 1: hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 15:1 last colon −3 (‘não precisais’ for ‘non eges’); 15:3 first colon +3 (the article and ‘estão’); 15:4b −4 / −3; 15:6 first colon +3 (‘lugares’ supplied for the neuter plural); 15:7 first colon −3; 15:8 second colon +5 (already shortened from +9 before any critic read it: ‘porque ele está à minha direita, para que eu não seja abalado’ → ‘porque está à minha direita, para eu não ser abalado’, the 118:80 build); 15:9 +3; 15:11 +3 / −4. No rhyme flag.

Draft 1. Two majors, nothing else; the marks confirmed. «A tradução conserva, nos demais versículos, o conteúdo e as imagens do latim, inclusive suas construções incomuns.» Passed in particular ‘Aos santos … fez maravilhosas’, ‘ajuntamentos’, ‘no inferno’, ‘deixareis o vosso santo ver a corrupção’, ‘deleites … até o fim’.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR: ‘de sangue’ loses the plural of de sanguínibus → ‘de sangues’
outcomes.reason: Held against a major. The glossary row vir sánguinum → ‘homem de sangue’ (5:7b; 25:9, 54:24, 138:19) loses the same plural, and one ruling must serve every place of the plural (with 50:16 de sanguínibus); ‘sangues’ is heard in Portuguese as a slip or as kinds of blood. The blind reader heard both readings of the plural (bloodshed, blood rites) in ‘de sangue’. His fix is an option; an open glossary row asks Gustavo.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR: ‘antevia’ brings in temporal foresight (Aulete) → ‘Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista’
outcomes.reason: The stylist and the blind reader (unknown word; ‘previa que veria’) agreed. His line exactly, in the Latin’s order.

note: Draft 1. Five verses; best 15:10, worst 15:3. «O salmo tem sobriedade e, em boa parte, já encontra uma voz de oração em português … as imagens incomuns, por si mesmas, não precisam ser suavizadas.» Two taken (one in part), three refused with options.

outcomes.remark: the opening hangs; ‘fez maravilhosas’ sounds carried over from the Latin → ‘Quanto aos santos …, tornou maravilhosas’ (worst line)
outcomes.reason: The hanging dative is the Latin’s (taken up by in eis); ‘Quanto aos’ decides grammar the Latin leaves open. ‘tornou’ refused for the glossary’s mirificáre → ‘fazer maravilhoso’ (4:4); both kept as options (sanctis, mirificavit). The blind reader heard the Lord as subject, as meant.

outcomes.remark: ‘lábios’ at the verse’s end is a proparoxytone → ‘nem pelos meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes’
outcomes.reason: His order taken (rule 4; D28); ‘com’ kept for per (the instrument), his ‘pelos’ an option.

outcomes.remark: ‘cálice’ at the mediant is a proparoxytone → ‘A parte da minha herança e do meu cálice é o Senhor’
outcomes.reason: The verse opens on Dóminus and turns to ‘sois vós’ — both colons open on the person; the proparoxytone accepted as at 90:1.

outcomes.remark: ‘e ainda até’ piles up particles; ‘ainda’ heard as duration → ‘e até a noite os meus rins também me repreenderam’
outcomes.reason: ínsuper et → ‘e ainda’ is the glossary’s, and 15:9 opens its last colon with the same words; ‘também’ breaks the pair. The slot widened so his line can be chosen.

outcomes.remark: ‘antevia’ suggests foreseeing the future → ‘Eu via sempre o Senhor diante de mim’
outcomes.reason: ‘via’ taken (with the Latinist); his ‘diante de mim’ refused — conspéctus keeps ‘vista’ (glossary, open) — and kept as an option.

note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. 24 items, 3 unknown words (congregarei, antevia, deleites). Tests: ‘no inferno’ heard first as the place of punishment, second as the realm of the dead — the risk the inferno decision named; ‘ver a corrupção’ heard first as moral corruption; ‘antevia’ heard as foreseeing (fixed); ‘fez maravilhosas’ heard with the Lord as subject; ‘os meus rins’ heard as the organs (the renes row foresaw it).

outcomes.remark: ‘em vós esperei’: hoped in you (heard first) / waited for you
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; speráre holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘meus bens’: possessions (heard first) / the good I have or do
outcomes.reason: bona holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘na sua terra’: the saints’ (heard first) / the Lord’s / the speaker’s
outcomes.reason: ejus is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘fez maravilhosas’: the Lord (heard first) / someone unnamed
outcomes.reason: Heard as meant; the Latin names no subject.

outcomes.remark: ‘todas as minhas vontades neles’: relation unclear
outcomes.reason: So is the Latin; kept, not explained.

outcomes.remark: ‘as enfermidades deles’: the saints’ (heard first) / another group
outcomes.reason: eórum is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘depois se apressaram’: the people (heard first, purpose unclear) / the infirmities
outcomes.reason: The Latin says no more.

outcomes.remark: ‘os seus ajuntamentos’: those of the previous verse (heard first) / the Lord’s
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘ajuntamentos de sangue’: bloodshed (heard first) / blood rites / pools of blood
outcomes.reason: The first two are the two readings of de sanguínibus; evidence for holding the singular.

outcomes.remark: ‘dos seus nomes’: the people’s (heard first) / the gatherings’
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘me lembrarei … com os meus lábios’: to pronounce (heard first) / remember silently
outcomes.reason: Heard as meant (and still so in draft 2’s order).

outcomes.remark: ‘a parte da minha herança e do meu cálice’: my portion (heard first; the cup unclear)
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s image; the cup is the psalter’s (10:7, 22:5).

outcomes.remark: ‘As cordas me caíram’: physical ropes (heard first) / measuring lines
outcomes.reason: funes → cordas (glossary); the image kept, not explained.

outcomes.remark: ‘até a noite’: until night (heard first) / even at night
outcomes.reason: usque ad noctem holds both; ‘até de noite’ is option 2.

outcomes.remark: ‘os meus rins me repreenderam’: the organs (heard first) / conscience
outcomes.reason: renes → rins (glossary, open): the organ named, as the row foresaw.

outcomes.remark: ‘antevia o Senhor’: foresaw (heard first) / saw before me
outcomes.reason: ‘via’ (with the Latinist and the stylist).

outcomes.remark: ‘não ser abalado’: physical / inner (heard first)
outcomes.reason: commovéri holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘a minha carne repousará’: body rests (heard first, possibly after death)
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘a minha alma no inferno’: place of punishment (heard first) / realm of the dead
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s word (D22), as Acts 2:27, 31; the verse promises the soul is not left there. For Gustavo’s ear (glossary row inférnus).

outcomes.remark: ‘o vosso santo’: the speaker / another, possibly Jesus (heard first)
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s ambiguity, and Acts 2:31’s reading.

outcomes.remark: ‘ver a corrupção’: moral corruption (heard first) / bodily decay
outcomes.reason: vidére corruptiónem is the Latin’s and Acts’ image; 15:9 (the flesh) and the first colon lean it to the body in prayer.

outcomes.remark: ‘com o vosso rosto’: the sight of it (heard first) / presence, favour
outcomes.reason: cum vultu tuo holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘na vossa direita’: the right hand (heard first) / the right side
outcomes.reason: in déxtera holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘até o fim’: end of the speaker’s life (heard first) / end of time
outcomes.reason: usque in finem holds both (D27: kept apart from in ætérnum).

outcomes.remark: unknown word: congregarei
outcomes.reason: congregáre’s own verb, one family with congregação.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: antevia
outcomes.reason: Replaced by ‘via’.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: deleites
outcomes.reason: delectátio’s word; ‘delícias’ is delíciæ’s (138:11) and option 2.

note: v2. Two verses changed against draft 1: 15:8 ‘Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista’ (was ‘antevia’; the Latinist’s major, with the stylist and the blind reader); 15:4b ‘nem com os meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes’ (the stylist’s order, rule 4). Slots widened so refused lines can be chosen: 15:5 (calicis, the whole first colon), 15:7 (noctem, with ‘e ainda’ and ‘os meus rins’), 15:4b (a ‘sangue’ slot under conventicula for the Latinist’s ‘de sangues’). HELD against the Latinist: 15:4b ‘de sangue’ (see the latinist step). Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the three v1 critics read). Script: ps015/revise_v2.py.
Draft 2: hard pass. Soft flags as draft 1 except 15:4b (−4 / −3, unchanged in count) and 15:8 first colon (13 against 15, no flag).

Draft 2 — the gate. One major, the same as draft 1’s and held on purpose: 15:4b ‘de sangue’ → ‘de sangues’. Nothing else; ‘Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista’ and ‘nem com os meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes’ passed; the marks confirmed.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR (repeated): ‘de sangue’ loses the plural of de sanguínibus → ‘de sangues’
outcomes.reason: Held, as at draft 1: one ruling for the plural across the psalter (vir sánguinum → homem de sangue), and ‘sangues’ heard as a slip. Put to Gustavo as an open glossary row; the fix is selectable.
